stem: A 62-year-old man is brought to the clinic for evaluation of a lump in his right chest. He reports that he first noticed the mass approximately four months ago and that it has slowly increased in size. He has a history of chronic liver disease and is currently taking a diuretic for edema. He reports no systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fever. On physical examination, his temperature is 36.8°C (98.6°F), pulse is 76/min, blood pressure is 138/84 mmHg, and respiratory rate is 14/min. Examination of the chest reveals a firm, non-tender, 2-cm mass located eccentrically to the right nipple. There is no evidence of skin dimpling or nipple retraction. No lymphadenopathy is noted in the axilla.
lead_in: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The patient presents with a firm, unilateral, eccentric subareolar mass. In men, the most common malignancy of the breast is invasive ductal carcinoma. This patient has a significant risk factor: cirrhosis (chronic liver disease), which leads to decreased estrogen clearance and an increased estrogen-to-androgen ratio, promoting breast tissue proliferation. Gynecomastia (A) typically presents as symmetric, centrally located, and soft/rubbery masses. Lipomas (C) are soft and mobile, and sebaceous cysts (D) typically have an opening to the skin. Tuberculous abscesses (E) would typically be associated with systemic symptoms like fever and weight loss, and would appear more inflammatory on examination.
teaching_point: Male breast cancer often presents as a firm, eccentric, subareolar mass and is associated with conditions that increase the estrogen-to-androgen ratio, such as cirrhosis or Klinefelter syndrome.

distractor_rationale.A: Typically symmetric, centrally located, and softer than a malignant mass.
distractor_rationale.C: Soft, mobile, and typically not located specifically in the subareolar region.
distractor_rationale.D: Cysts are usually superficial and may have a central punctum.
distractor_rationale.E: Would likely present with fever, night sweats, and an inflammatory or fluctuant mass.
